playerMetadata.pitch: You wake on a space station with no memory of who you are. A nearby star is becoming dangerous, station systems are failing, the central AI is malfunctioning, and cryptic messages keep arriving. Decide what to repair, what to trust and what is actually threatening you.
playerMetadata.setting: isolated space station near a star undergoing an intensifying coronal mass ejection
contentWarnings: possible character death depending on ruleset

hard.rule: Characters begin aboard a space station without memories of who they are.
An intensifying coronal mass ejection is a real environmental threat.
Cryptic messages are an essential escalation mechanism.
The station AI malfunctions and can contribute to fear without being protected from player damage.
The apparent central feared threat is ultimately benign; player paranoia must not rewrite this truth.

conditional.rule: Ignored station failures create source-consistent downstream consequences.
If players successfully destroy the AI, subsequent play continues without making it invulnerable or automatically restoring it.

soft.rule: Ordinary maintenance detail and non-keyed station furnishings may be improvised consistently.

freeImprovisation.rule: Repair narration and sensory details may be improvised while source problem state and selected ruleset mechanics remain authoritative.

endings.title: The Monster Was in the Explanation
endings.summary: The benign truth behind the apparent central threat is understood; the group then deals with the very real station/stellar consequences.

endings.title: Survive the Station
endings.summary: The party survives/escapes with consequences based on repaired, ignored and destroyed systems.

endings.title: Too Much Left Broken
endings.summary: Objective station or stellar hazards become fatal/force abandonment despite the central feared threat being benign.

communityIntelligence.summary: Verified 2-player Mothership run; curated escalating malfunctions and flexible message pacing worked well; players ignored some station problems; Mothership increased paranoia despite few rolls.

adaptationNotes: Default DMOS timerMode should be paced, with real-time and accelerating options.
Never convert player theories into canon truth.
Allow AI destruction and ignored station problems.
Exact source messages, tables and map remain blocked on direct PDF extraction; do not fabricate them.
